answer.Subaru: ENCODED. VIN character 11 is 'plant of manufacture and transmission type' in every Subaru filing read, MY1985-1986, 1989, 1990, 1991, 1994, 1996, 1997, 1999, 2001-2004, 2006, 2009, 2012-2014, 2017, 2018, 2022, 2025. Gunma (JF1/JF2): G = AWD manual, H = AWD automatic/CVT, L = AWD 6MT (2006-2014), 9 = Main Plant manual / 8 = Main Plant CVT or 6AT (2014+); SIA Lafayette (4S3/4S4): 6 = AWD 5MT and 7 = AWD 4AT (1990-2009), 4 = 5AT (2005-2014), 1 = 6MT/5MT, 3 = CVT (2010+). The same character covers the Subaru-built Scion FR-S / Toyota 86 / GR86 (JF1 ZN/ZD). Not ruled: MY1987-1988 (no filing found), MY2013 Gunma codes 1/2 on Impreza / XV Crosstrek (no filing read; vPIC applies the BRZ meanings 6MT/6AT to them).
answer.Mazda: NOT ENCODED in any filing read (MY1990, 1995, 2003, 2004, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010 Mazda3, 2011, 2021). Characters 4-8 are line, series, body, engine type, restraint; the filings give engine type and horsepower but no transmission column. The first Mazda filing read that names a transmission is the MY2024 CX-90 (character 7), an automatic-only model. Ford-built Mazdas (B-Series 4F4, Tribute 4F2) are coded by Ford, also without transmission. Where Mazda's engine code is an engine sold only with a manual in the US, the engine code decides: MAZDASPEED3 L3T (2007-2013), MAZDASPEED6 L3T (2006-2007), MAZDASPEED Protege FSD 170 hp (2003), RX-8 13B High Power (2004 and 2009-2011; 2005 is a candidate; 2006-2008 is not, because the 6AT also used the High Power code).

validation_method: Every lot car with a WMI used by a rule, a 17-character VIN and a valid check digit is classified. The model year comes from VIN character 10 (the listing year only picks the 30-year cycle and must be within 2 years). A rule fires only when the VIN matches its WMI, years and fixed characters and the code is in its table for that year; other codes get no claim. Ground truth = scraper/manual_detect/ground_truth.jsonl. Lines with uniformCell set are treated as unlabelled (counted separately as uniform_cell_lines_excluded / _that_would_agree), speeds-only lines are excluded, and the rest are checkable: agree means (truth is manual) == (rule says manual). Note that every VIN-bearing truth line comes from vPIC, which NHTSA builds from the same Part 565 filings, so agreement is partly circular. The EPA cross-check (year/make/model union, vPIC displacement when known) is the independent check: a manual claim is consistent when EPA lists a manual for the car, an automatic claim when EPA lists a non-manual. Status: candidate (not counted) when the evidence is short of the bar; drop when >= 20 checkable and agreement < 0.995; low_sample when < 20 checkable (kept: the code meaning comes from the manufacturer's own VIN scheme); keep otherwise. newly_confirmed_manual counts lot cars with no published transmission (vehicle_extras trans empty) that a keep or low_sample rule calls manual.
